column1: # OCaml. A definition is an item of the file, or of a module or signature written in the file,
# at any depth of modules, `include struct` / `include sig` / `include module type of struct`,
# `open struct`, constrained modules (`module M : sig ... end with type t := u`) and functor
# parameter and result signatures. An item with an expression above it is not one: see below.
#   let / let rec / and: function when it has parameters or its body is fun or function,
#     variable otherwise (so `let pi = 3.14` and `let tm = structure "tm"` are variables);
#     a parenthesised operator is named by the operator; `let () =`, `let _ =` and tuple
#   val (.mli or sig): function when the type is a function type, variable otherwise;
#   type -> class for a variant, record, abstract or extensible type, type_alias for an alias;
#   exception -> class; module -> package; module type -> interface;
#   class -> class, class type -> interface, method -> method, instance variable (val) -> field.
# Not definitions: let ... in inside an expression, let module (and everything in it), the
# argument of a functor application (`Make (struct let seed = 1 end)`), a destructive
# substitution (`type t := u`, in a signature or after `with`), variant constructors, record
